content:
MS NOW host Rachel Maddow on Monday decried all the AI-generated so-called slop proliferating online, as even President Donald Trump has now posted a “totally fake” news segment on social media — featuring a completely fabricated monologue of hers.

“This is an AI-generated video with a totally fake AI-generated narration by a totally fake AI-generated me,” Maddow said Monday. “It sounds like my voice. That is not me. And that video is about something I have never talked about and would never talk about.”

She explained, “The video is, I kid you not, about how the Chinese people love Donald Trump so much and they love their own president, too. And the reason I’m showing you this at all is because this video was posted today by the president of the United States.”

Maddow played an excerpt of the “slop” video depicting Trump being driven around Shenzhen during his recent visit to China, with her AI-generated voice proclaiming “the media will never show you this” clip of “hundreds of thousands of people cheering for him.”

“And they love Trump!” Maddow’s voice continued. “They say so in interviews. They said it is like hitting a lottery ticket. They said it is just something that they traveled five hours to see. It’s like winning millions in the lottery. Crowds outside of his hotel were waiting to see Trump.”

There weren’t “hundreds of thousands of people” cheering for Trump, however, nor did Maddow ever produce a segment on the comments from onlookers. She noted there’s “a ton” of “AI slop” using her likeness that her team is regularly flagging to be taken down.

Trump has been a staunch supporter of AI and the data centers needed to process its burgeoning use, calling them “LIQUID GOLD” in taxes and job creation — despite polls showing Republicans and Democrats alike oppose data center construction where they live.

Maddow said Monday there’s typically a telltale sign that the “gross” content depicting her is fake, namely that it will have her discussing something she never has before — and is usually something “that might only resonate politically in a foreign country.”

“I will tell you that the TikTok account where the video originated, an account that had Vietnamese text at the top and had posted dozens of AI-generated videos narrated by fake me, TikTok has taken down that account tonight after we reached out to them,” said Maddow.

The MS NOW host concluded Monday, “But still, that one video is still up one place — on President Donald Trump’s social media site. We’ve asked the White House for comment. We’ll let you know if we hear anything back.”
